source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Brakes, p.5-22

procedures.title: Brake pipe distribution and switch assembly: remove and install
parts: brake pipe distribution and switch assembly
steps: Unplug the electrical lead from the switch.
Put dry rags under the switch for spilled fluid.
Disconnect the 4 brake lines at the switch, loosening the line nuts at the main cylinder if needed; cover the open line ends with clean lint-free material.
Remove the mounting screw and take out the switch.
(Installation) Make sure the new switch is free of dust and lint; if unsure, wash it in Declene or equivalent and air dry.
Fasten the switch to its bracket with the mounting screw.
Uncover the lines and connect them to the switch; tighten the line nuts at the main cylinder if they were loosened.
notes: The pressure differential warning switch cannot be adjusted or repaired; replace it if faulty.
Figure 2 in the manual shows Chevrolet and Camaro installations. Drum installation and the Camaro pressure regulator valve on this page are not included.

procedures.title: Brake warning light: check
steps: Set and release the parking brake to prove the bulb works.
Make sure both main cylinder reservoirs are full.
Open the bleed screw at one rear wheel.
Press and hold the brake pedal; the light should come on from the front/rear pressure difference.
Close the bleed screw, then let the pedal up. Top up the rear reservoir if needed.

specs.what: pressure differential to light brake warning lamp

notes: Take care not to let air into the system while checking the switch.
Check every 24 months or 24,000 miles, after any major brake work, or when the owner reports excessive pedal travel.
